articles.title: When random is not actually random enough
articles.summary: A common pattern in codebases is to pick a random object from a set, with each object having an equal chance of being chosen. However, this approach can lead to a non-uniform distribution of the chosen object, as the probability of each object being picked is not preserved. This is evident when using a simple modulo-based approach, where the chosen object is picked based on a random number generated from a uniform distribution. This can result in the chosen object being picked more frequently than intended, such as 40% of the time when using the `random_u64()` function. A more complex solution, such as the `random_between()` function, provides a more uniform distribution by giving each inclusive number between a specified range a 1/((range - lower_bound) + 1) chance of being picked, which is a more intuitive and mentally correct approach.
